Subject: Perimeter and Provisioning Runbook Kickoff — SSO, SCIM, IP & Service Accounts

Hi Alex / Platform team,

Thanks again for partnering with Redwood — excited to get the access controls portion of the onboarding moving. Attached are the two templates we'll use during the kickoff: network-allowlist-template.csv (simple CIDR list) and provisioning-playbook-v1.pdf (sequence + checks). I've also attached a blank SCIM mapping sheet.

Proposed agenda for the kickoff (30–45m):
- Confirm SAML IdP metadata and required attributes (email, name, groups)
- SCIM: group push vs. sync, attribute mapping, initial user set
- IP allowlist / egress ranges for Dedicated & Private (we'll need your firewall rules)
- Service accounts: scopes, key rotation cadence, and where RDW-managed pods will run
- Rollout cadence and responsible owners (MediSys, Redwood, Cloud infra)

Can you confirm availability for a kickoff on Wednesday 2027-04-28 at 10:00 PT? If that doesn't work, please propose two alternative slots. Also please bring (or reply with) the following prior to the call:
- SAML metadata URL or IdP certificate
- Any current CIDR list you expect to allow to Redwood (we'll accept a CSV using the attached template)
- Any SCIM group naming conventions you rely on

Next steps on our side: Marissa will coordinate network engineering items and Jonas will confirm the egress IP set for Dedicated. Neha will own provisioning and service account policy.

Attachments: network-allowlist-template.csv, provisioning-playbook-v1.pdf, scim-attributes-mapping.xlsx

Thanks,

Rafael Mendes
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

Hi Rafael / team,

Thanks — Wednesday 4/28 at 10:00 PT works for us. I'll be on the call along with our platform lead (platform@medisys.io). A couple of prep items/questions from our security side:

- For SAML, our IdP supports sending attributes: mail, givenName, sn, and memberOf. Do you require a specific attribute name for groups (we currently use memberOf)?
- SCIM: we typically push group memberships from our IdP; does Redwood support group push (not just user provisioning)?
- For service accounts, please confirm the minimum required scopes/roles you need on our side so we can provision least-privilege accounts (and whether we should create a long-lived key or use short-lived credentials).
- We'll pull our current egress CIDR list and send it by EOB tomorrow (FYI it will include a mix of office subnets and cloud NATs).

Also, can you share a short checklist for the internal teams we should have on the call (network, identity, application owners)?

Alex Kim
Director, Security Engineering
MediSys
security@medisys.io
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <security@medisys.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Perimeter and Provisioning Runbook Kickoff — SSO, SCIM, IP & Service Accounts

Great — confirmed for 2027-04-28 10:00 PT. Quick answers to your questions and a proposed sequencing below so platform can prep.

SAML attributes: we accept memberOf for groups; preferred attribute mapping is:
- email -> mail (or email)
- name -> givenName + sn (or name combined)
- groups -> memberOf

SCIM: Redwood supports group push (we will sync groups and group memberships). The attached scim-attributes-mapping.xlsx contains our recommended mappings and a short column for "required/optional" — please fill that out.

Service accounts: recommend creating a service account with a scoped role that allows provisioning to your identity provider and access to the specific org/project you'll assign. For Dedicated customers we typically request:
- Read/Write to the SCIM endpoint (HTTPS)
- Ability to fetch SAML metadata if you host metadata behind auth
- Network egress to our IP ranges (we'll provide exact CIDRs)

Network / sequencing (proposed):
1) Pre-kickoff: MediSys sends SAML metadata URL, initial CIDR CSV, and a filled SCIM mapping (by 4/27 EOB)
2) Kickoff (4/28): align on owners, sign off on mapping, confirm service account plan
3) Post-kickoff (within 3 business days): Redwood creates a test service account, validates SCIM sync to a staging org, and shares test user provisioning evidence
4) Production flip planned after smoke tests and a scheduled maintenance window

Prep participants we recommend on the call: network engineer, identity owner (IdP admin), platform lead, application owner (someone who owns user-group contracts). I'll attach the provisioning playbook link here for your team: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBcdExample

Marissa — can you confirm the egress IPs we expect to provide for Dedicated and whether we have a single static range or multiple ranges per region? Jonas, looping you to confirm.

Thanks,

Rafael
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Quick internal note for the thread — we'll provide the standard Dedicated egress CIDR set for the US region: 54.183.16.0/20 and 34.201.12.0/22 (these are the ranges we typically ask customers to allow). Jonas, please confirm if any additional outbound ports/hosts are needed for telemetry.

Alex — for the kickoff, please have your IdP admin populate the SCIM mapping sheet and attach the SAML metadata URL. That will let Neha run the staging sync within 24–48 hours after the call.

Also: small ask from procurement/CS — because this is on the RDW Dedicated track (deal RDW-5832), please be prepared to sign the provisioning addendum after we validate the staging test. We'll route the DocuSign after the smoke tests.

Thanks everyone — see you on 4/28.

Marissa Cole
